paragraphs: Rav Huna bar Natan pressed Rav Ashi aside, for he ruled after Rav Ashi (see his entry). In Eruvin 42b and Yoma 87, end of side b: son of Rav Natan; he deferred to Rav Ashi (see his entry). Rav Ashi said, “Huna ben Natan told me: I asked Rava’s scribes”: Bava Batra 55a. Amemar permitted him to marry a woman of Mechoza; Amemar had heard from Rav Zevid of Nehardea: Kiddushin 72b. He stood before King Izgadar, who adjusted his sash for him. Amemar said to him, “In you has been fulfilled, ‘Kings shall be your foster fathers’”: Zevachim chapter 2, 19a. And Rav Geviha of Argiza (see Merimar). Rav Nachman said, “Huna ben Natan told me”: Ketubbot 7, end of side a. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak asked him, “What is your name?” He answered, “I am a man with a title.” Rashi explains: from his youth they called him “ben Rav Huna”; Rabbenu Chananel explains that they ordained him and called him Rav Huna. See Chiddushei Aggadot, Pesachim 86b. Rav Natan was his father (see his entry). He said to Rav Pappa, “Does the master not hold …?” Berakhot 42a. Rav Huna bar Natan said to Rav Pappa: Pesachim 17b; Zevachim 41b, 45b; see Menachot 15a. He spoke to Rava: Nedarim 12, beginning of side a. This requires examination: he spoke with Rava, on whose death-day Rav Ashi was born, and with Rav Nachman, Rava’s teacher. Presumably he was grown then, since he stated a law to Rav Nachman; Rav Ashi lived at least seventy-four years (see his entry). How did he rule after Rav Ashi? Perhaps he was extremely old; therefore he pressed Rav Ashi aside. Some places also say Rav Huna bar Natan, and some bar Rav Natan. Perhaps there were two; requires examination.
